title: A Profile the Machine Can Follow: Where the Setpoint Comes From

questions.question: A one metre move is commanded as a step, and again through a trapezoidal profile with feedforward. What happens to the peak command?
options: 20.2 N for the step and 1.4 N for the profile, because a step asks for an infinite velocity
About the same, since the same distance is covered
Higher for the profile, since it also feeds forward
It depends only on the gains
questions.explanation: The peak for a step is set by the gain rather than by anything about the machine or the move. The gains are not the problem: a step turns every commanded move into a disturbance.

questions.question: With a top speed of 0.5 m/s and an acceleration of 1 m/s^2, what is the shortest move that reaches the top speed?
options: 0.25 m, which is top speed squared over the acceleration, and it is an exact boundary
0.5 m, the top speed times one second
1.0 m, from the acceleration
It depends on the distance travelled while cruising
questions.explanation: That is what speeding up and slowing down again costs. Just below it there is no cruise phase and the profile is a triangle whose peak is sqrt(acceleration times distance).

questions.question: A planner assumes three phases and is given a 0.10 m move. What does it do?
options: Computes a cruise time of -0.3 s, arrives at exactly 0.10 m with zero velocity, and drops the commanded velocity by 0.3 m/s between two adjacent instants
Divides by zero and crashes
Overshoots the target and comes back
Refuses the move
questions.explanation: An endpoint test passes. The fault is entirely in the middle: an instantaneous 0.3 m/s change is an infinite acceleration, and precisely the thing a profile exists to prevent.

questions.question: What test catches that, when an endpoint test does not?
options: Sampling the commanded velocity finely and asserting no two adjacent samples differ by more than the profile's own acceleration times the interval
Checking the total duration against a formula
Checking that the position is monotonic
Running the profile through the control loop and watching the error
questions.explanation: Anything larger is an acceleration the profile never promised. One loop, and it also needs a move shorter than top speed squared over the acceleration, which is most of the moves a robot actually makes.

questions.question: A singularity limits how fast one direction of a path can be driven. What should slow down?
options: The whole profile in time: stretching by a factor divides every velocity by it and every acceleration by its square, preserving the shape exactly
Only the limited direction
The acceleration limit only
Nothing; the loop should absorb it
questions.explanation: The shape of a path is the relationship between its axes at each instant. Scale one and it becomes a different path with the same endpoints. For several axes, take the longest time any of them needs and stretch them all to it.

questions.question: scaled_to is asked for a duration shorter than the profile's own. What should it return?
options: The profile unchanged: the machine cannot do it, and handing back something it cannot follow moves the failure downstream
A profile at the requested duration, with higher limits
A profile with the acceleration raised and the top speed kept
An empty profile
questions.explanation: The other two cases to get right are a move of zero, where the direction is undefined, and a move backwards, which is the same profile with every sign turned round.
